newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 27.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In his meeting with United States President Bill Clinton in Washington today, Prime Minister John Howard will adopt a new tactic in his fight against uniform greenhouse gas reduction targets. Howard is hoping to persuade Clinton that Australia's proposal for "differentiation" of developed nations' greenhouse targets can satisfy US demands that developing countries be included in anti-pollution measures. Page 1.

Health funds, including Medibank Private, National Mutual Health Insurance, and MBF are reporting a rush of inquiries from prospective and existing members before the Federal Government's tax changes come into effect next Tuesday. Page 1.

After yesterday admitting he played a significant role in managing his private companies since being in office, Federal Small Business Minister Geoff Prosser was accused by the Opposition of breaching Prime Minister John Howard's code of conduct, which dos not allow daily involvement in business affairs. Page 5.

The latest quarterly survey from the Australian Chamber of Manufacturers, which covers more than 600 manufacturing companies, shows uncertainty caused by the Federal Government's approach to industry policy has led to another drop in manufacturing output.Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Federal Small Business Minister Geoff Prosser has survived Opposition attempts to get him dismissed after detailing the meetings he has been involved in since becoming a minister. Prosser's revelations see him face further conflict of interest allegation, as the Opposition yesterday said his actions have breached prime ministerial guidelines which prevent him from engaging in the daily running of a business. Page 1.

Bruno Gordano Grollo was yesterday cleared of charges of conspiring to pervert a tax fraud investigation in Victoria's County Court. Grollo said his family has suffered tremendously since the charges were laid four years ago, and he invoked the tall poppy syndrome for his "relentless persecution". Page 1.

In a paper on gender, sexualities and sport she prepared for Victoria University, historian Margaret Lindsay says it is sex that sells the Australian Football League, quoting League statistics which show 50 per cent of crowds at the games are female. Page 1.

The national council of the Australian Manufacturing Workers Union yesterday called on the ACTU to co-ordinate a national campaign against any introduction of a goods and services tax on the basis that employers may face higher wage claims to compensate for any inflationary impact of a GST. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In a long statement, Prime Minister John Howard has warned Small Business Minister Geoff Prosser that he may lose his job if there are any further revelations about his business affairs, after he was ordered to tell Parliament all his business involvements. However, it would appear that the material Prosser provided to Parliament may have added more fuel to Opposition calls for his resignation. Page 1.

The New South Wales Government Committee on Treasury and Energy yesterday voted against State Treasurer Michael Egan's plans to privatise the State's A$22 billion electricity industry. The vote goes against Egan's vow that the committee would fight for te privatisation, with one member saying the community was more concerned about jobs. Page 1.

Despite Australia's tariff-free entry into New Zealand under the Closer Economic Relations agreement, the nation's A$500 million annual car exports to New Zealand are under threat after an announcement in New Zealand's Budget that there would be a "swift removal" of tariffs on non-Australian imports. Page 1.

A report of 10 of New South Wales' largest institutions released yesterday by New South Wales Community Services Minister Roger West has revealed disabled people are living in violent conditions where drugs are used as chemical restraints and human dignit is ignored. Page 1.
THE AGE

Melbourne property developer Bruno Grollo last night celebrated his victory against conspiracy charges after being acquitted in the County Court. Grollo attacked Australia's criminal justice system, saying the 13-month trial had dogged his family and had caused them enormous pain and fear. Page 1.

The Federal Health Department is investigating medical trials on more than 160 Victorian girls in the 1950s to 1970s to try to stop them growing tall. The trials, partly funded by the National Health and Medical Research Council, saw girls given a sex homone which was later linked to vaginal cancer. Page 1.

The Victorian Forensic Science Laboratory last night seized and examined a car belonging to Greg Domaszewicz, who was babysitting 14-month-old Jaidyn Leskie on the night the toddler disappeared. Detective Senior Sergeant Rowland Legg was unable to confirm why the car had been seized. Page 2.

Environment and community groups yesterday described the vent stacks for the two City Link tunnels as a health risk, especially for children, and attacked the Environmental Protection for their design. The Authority approved the design of the stacks two weeks ago. Page 3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
